TWO FINDINGS WORTH STEALING. ONE, A STALE BUILD ARTIFACT CAN MAKE A TEST LIE. A reviewer mutated a constant to prove a test could fail, then restored the file WITHOUT advancing its mtime. Cargo fingerprint saw no change and every later run re-executed the binary built from the MUTATED source, so a full suite reported a good test failing while the source on disk was correct. touch fixed it. The dangerous direction is the opposite one: a mutation that makes a test PASS, restored the same way, leaves a stale binary reporting green over broken source, which is silent and indistinguishable from real evidence. This repo already says restore from a copy rather than git checkout dash-dash; it does not yet say the restore must ADVANCE THE MTIME, or that a mutation probe should be followed by touch before the next run is trusted.
